entities.summary: The Constitution of the Arab Republic of Egypt was the former constitution of Egypt. It was adopted on 11 September 1971 through a public referendum. It was later amended in 1980, 2005, and 2007. It was proclaimed to update the democratic representative system in assertion of the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and party plurality. On 13 February 2011, the Constitution was suspended following the resignation of President Hosni Mubarak as a result of the 2011 Egyptian Revolution. On 30 March 2011, it was "effectively voided" after a new provisional constitution was passed by the country's ruling Supreme Council of the Armed Forces.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Egyptian Constitution of 1971 played a significant role in shaping Egypt's political landscape, particularly during the country's transition to democracy after the 2011 Egyptian Revolution. Its suspension and eventual voiding paved the way for a new era of governance.
